name: Lijiang Sanyi International Airport
before:
The airport for Lijiang in Yunnan, 25 km south of the city, and one of the clearest examples of Chinese domestic tourism at work. It handled 8,631,218 passengers in 2025, against 4.2 million in 2021.

That growth has outrun the building more than once. The airport opened in July 1995 with a 2,500 metre runway. The Kunming World Horticultural Exposition in 1999 pushed it past half a million passengers for the first time and triggered the first expansion. A second, in 2007, added 500 metres of runway, a parallel taxiway, thirteen more stands and a 33,300 square metre domestic terminal, all built to a 4.5 million passenger standard it has long since passed.

The runway now measures 3,000 metres with turning bases at both ends. The airport was cleared for international traffic in March 2012, the third in Yunnan to hold that status.
after:
The airport for Lijiang in Yunnan, 25 km south of the city. It has grown on the back of Lijiang's tourism, and in 2025 it handled 8,631,218 passengers, up 6.7 per cent on 2024.

That growth has outrun the building more than once. It opened in July 1995, and the Kunming World Horticultural Exposition in 1999 pushed it past half a million passengers for the first time and triggered the first expansion. A second, begun at the end of 2007, left it with the 3,000 metre runway it has today.

The airport opened to international traffic in 2012.

China News Service (2013) says the fast growth of Lijiang's tourism market drove the airport's golden period and that the second expansion was built to meet it; Wikipedia ties the first growth spurt to the 1999 Expo and Lijiang tourism.

claims.claim: one of the clearest examples of Chinese domestic tourism at work
claims.wasBefore: one of the clearest examples of Chinese domestic tourism at work
claims.why: No source describes it so, and nothing current gives the domestic share. Softened to its growth on Lijiang's tourism (see above).

Replaced by the latest year-on-year comparison (see above). 2021 sits in the dip of the pandemic years (Wikipedia's own series: 4.22 million in 2021, 2.88 million in 2022, 7.44 million in 2023), so set against 2025 it overstated the growth.

claims.wasBefore: The airport opened in July 1995 with a 2,500 metre runway.
claims.why: The opening month is kept (see above); the 2,500 m rests on Wikipedia alone, as China News Service gives only the 3,000 m after the second expansion.

claims.claim: the 2007 expansion's 500 m of runway, parallel taxiway, 13 more stands and 33,300 m2 domestic terminal
claims.wasBefore: added 500 metres of runway, a parallel taxiway, thirteen more stands and a 33,300 square metre domestic terminal
claims.why: Wikipedia alone for the taxiway and the 13 more stands (China News Service gives 19 stands in all afterwards). The domestic terminal's size disagrees: 33,300 square metres (Wikipedia) or 33,000 (China News Service). The runway's end state is kept (see above).

claims.claim: built to a 4.5 million passenger standard it has long since passed
claims.wasBefore: all built to a 4.5 million passenger standard it has long since passed
claims.why: Wikipedia and a Baidu Baike text copied onto the airport's advertising site (lijiangairport.com), which is not good enough for a capacity claim; nothing current says what the building is rated for now. The operator's own site (lijiang-airport.com) answered 503.

claims.wasBefore: with turning bases at both ends

claims.claim: cleared in March 2012, third in Yunnan
claims.wasBefore: The airport was cleared for international traffic in March 2012, the third in Yunnan to hold that status.
claims.why: The month depends on which step is meant (approval November 2011, acceptance March 2012, first Hong Kong flight May 2012), so only the year is kept (see above). 'The third in Yunnan' rests on Wikipedia alone.

opinion.text: That growth has outrun the building more than once.
opinion.why: The old text's judgement, kept: China News Service says the first expansion followed the 1999 jump in traffic and the second was built to meet the fast growth of Lijiang's tourism.
